title: Pairs of Blocks That Are Anagrams

concept.title: A hash that does not depend on the order of the letters
body: Two blocks are anagrams when they have the same letter counts. A rolling hash that depends on letter **order** is no help here. Instead give every letter a **random-looking 64-bit number** `val[c]` and define the key of a block as the **sum** of the values of its letters (modulo 2^64). A sum does not care about order, so anagrams get equal keys. Different letter counts give different sums with overwhelming probability.

body.code:
val[c] = mix(c + 1)               # a scrambling function makes the 26 numbers look random
window += val[new letter] - val[old letter]   # sliding the block by one: O(1)

body: This is called **Zobrist hashing**. For every block length `L`, slide a block over the word, collect the keys, and count the groups of equal keys: a group of `c` equal keys gives `c * (c - 1) / 2` pairs. The "scrambling function" is needed: with plain numbers such as 1, 2, 3 the sums of different letter counts collide all the time.

statement: Count the pairs of blocks of consecutive letters that have the same length, start at different positions, and are anagrams of each other (they consist of the same letters with the same counts, in any order). Blocks may overlap. Block lengths from 1 up to the length of the word minus 1 are considered.
inputFormat: A single word of lowercase letters.

examples.note: Length 1: the two a and the two b give 2 pairs. Length 2: ab, bb, ba: ab and ba are anagrams: 1 pair. Length 3: abb and bba: 1 pair. Total 4.

hints: A block key must not depend on the order of the letters: use the sum of a random number per letter.
For each length, slide a block over the word and keep the key up to date in O(1).
For every group of `c` equal keys add `c * (c - 1) / 2` pairs.

explanation: The sum of a random 64-bit number per letter is a key that ignores the order of the letters. For every length the keys of the blocks are grouped and each group of `c` blocks gives `c * (c - 1) / 2` pairs.
solution.complexity: Time O(n^2 log n), space O(n).
